ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (Prevención del Uso del Sistema Financiero para el Blanqueo de Capitales, el Financiamiento del Terrorismo y el Financiamiento de la Proliferación de Armas de Destrucción Masiva), as amended; Executive Decree No. 363 of 2015; Regulation SIB-004-2016 of the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá; Ley No. 129 de 28 de mayo de 2020 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales); and the implementing regulations and forms issued by the Registro Público de Panamá and the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only if a certificate issued abroad is appended; otherwise execution before Panamanian Notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-Country Companies Registry or the Home-Country Registered Agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public, Official Civil Registry, Embassy, or Consulate in the Document Holder's Country of Origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney Granted to the Panamanian Registered Agent / Formation Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the Home Country or Panamanian Notary Public if executed in Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ultimate Beneficial Owner Sworn Declaration (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Notary Public through the Registered Agent, submitted to the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Executed before a Panamanian Notary and electronically filed in the Registry of Final Beneficiaries

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, foundation council members, beneficiaries, officers, and any person exercising significant control against the Panamanian Unidad de Análisis Financiero lists, the National Police of Panama terrorist lists, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and UK HMT consolidated sanctions list. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, senior management approval, and enhanced transaction monitoring. The same standard applies to entities from high-risk and non-cooperative jurisdictions. Records must be retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ventanilla Única Electrónica del Registro Público de Panamá (Sistema de Reserva de Nombre de Fundaciones de Interés Privado) at the official portal of the Registro Público de Panamá
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names must be expressed in Spanish or in a foreign language transliterated into the Spanish alphabet. The registrars require Spanish customary naming conventions; if a trademark or foreign word is used, an additional Spanish descriptive clause must be included in the Foundation Charter. The foundation's corporate object may contain English or Chinese terms only if a Spanish translation of the object is also properly established.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the chosen foundation name is rejected, the applicant or its registered agent receives a written rejection notice from the Registro Público. Within five business days from notification, the interested party may file a reconsideration petition ('recurso de reconsideración') before the same registry officer. If denied, a hierarchical appeal ('recurso de apelación') may be lodged with the General Director of the Registro Público within five business days from the adverse decision, under the Administrative Procedure Law (Ley 38 de 2000). A new name reservation may also be submitted immediately without prejudice to the appeal. The reserved name is not renewable; upon expiry another applicant may reserve the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual office without a physical Panamanian address is not acceptable for the statutory foundation registered office. The Private Interest Foundation must maintain a registered office and permanent registered agent in Panama. Virtual administrative back-office services and digital record-keeping are permitted, but the restaurant operations require physical premises for the Ministry of Health (MINSA) operating license, Panama Fire Department (DICOM) inspection, and municipal business licence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Regime), as amended by Ley No. 41 de 2014 and Ley No. 52 de 2016; regulated by Decreto Ejecutivo No. 11 de 22 de mayo de 1996; applicable sections: Arts. 4-15 (constitution and registration), Arts. 17-21 (Foundation Council), Arts. 22-32 (patrimony, beneficiaries, and registered agent).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Dirección General del Registro Público, Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva (Foundation Charter / Deed of Constitution) executed before a Panamanian Notary Public and filed for inscription in the Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado; the Reglamento (private Bylaws) may be executed and retained confidentially by the Foundation Council.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Ley 25 de 1995 requires the Foundation Charter to declare an initial endowment (dotación inicial) of at least US$10,000 in cash or assets, transferred or pledged by the Founder; no statutory escrow or paid-up bank deposit is mandated, but the endowment must be evidenced in the Charter and the Resident Agent must maintain source-of-funds records for AML due diligence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME] - Adopted by unanimous written consent at Panama City on [date]. The Foundation Council, duly registered, resolves: 1. To ratify the initial endowment of minimum USD 10,000 contributed by the Founder and to accept title to the endowed assets per Schedule A. 2. To adopt the Resident Agent's Panama address as the Foundation's registered office and to confirm the Resident Agent's appointment. 3. To appoint the Council as the governing board and to elect [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer, with administrative powers exercised jointly or severally. 4. To authorize the President to execute corporate forms and banking instructions to implement this resolution. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Resident Agent and Pre-Incorporation Name Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian attorney acting as Resident Agent; preliminary name check at the Registro Público de Panamá through the public registry name-search service (Geoportal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute an engagement letter with a Resident Agent authorized under Ley 25 de 1995. Instruct the agent to verify the proposed foundation name (primary and reserve names) against existing registrations and to prepare the draft Acta Constitutiva and private Reglamento in Spanish/English, including founder details, council members, beneficiary clauses, endowment statement, registered office, and duration.
required_dossiers: Founder's certified passport copy and proof of address
Beneficiaries' identification details
Foundation Council members' names, nationalities, and identification
Proposed foundation names (primary and reserve)
Statement of initial endowment (minimum USD 10,000) and description of assets
Bank reference or source-of-funds letter for AML due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing registration, the Resident Agent resubmits the alternate name at no additional registry fee; incomplete due diligence documents are cured by issuing a deficiency letter to the founder with a 5-business-day response window before drafting resumes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Foundation Charter and Bylaws Before a Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público (Public Notary) authorized by the Corte Suprema de Justicia; protocols administered under Panamanian notarial rules.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder executes the Acta Constitutiva in Spanish before the notary. The notary witnesses signatures, certifies legal capacity, records the act in the notarial protocol, issues certified copies, and collects stamp taxes (timbres). The Reglamento is executed separately and retained privately by the Foundation Council to preserve confidentiality.
required_dossiers: Final draft of the Acta Constitutiva
Reglamento (private bylaws)
Founder's original passport
Notary fee and stamp tax payment receipt
Resident Agent's written acceptance of appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies an inconsistency between the declaration and the endowment or asset clause, the parties sign an amendment (adenda) or rectification (aclaración) instrument before registration; corrections are completed within the same engagement without additional professional fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation at the Public Registry (Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, including digital and physical filing counters at the Central Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized charter, together with two certified copies and the registry fee receipt. The Registry conducts legal review (calificación registral), verifies compliance with Ley 25 de 1995 and its amendments, and issues the inscription (ficha registral). The Foundation becomes a separate legal person effective from the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Acta Constitutiva (original plus two certified copies)
Registry fee payment receipt (timbres and tasas)
Resident Agent's petition signed by an attorney
Council members' written acceptance letters
Power of attorney if the Resident Agent acts on behalf of the Founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues an observación (defect notice), the Resident Agent corrects and resubmits within the statutory 30-day term; if rejected, the Foundation files a recurso de reconsideración within 5 business days and then a recurso de apelación to the Director General of the Public Registry; judicial cure before the competent civil court remains available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Foundation Certificate and Organizational Council Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Certification Office) and the Foundation Council as the governing body.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the certified certificate of inscription (Certificado de Fundación) and certified copies of the registered charter. Convene the Foundation Council to execute the First Board Resolution covering office adoption, officer appointments, and banking signatories; open the corporate minute ledger (Libro de Actas).
required_dossiers: Inscription certificate (Certificado de Fundación)
Certified copy of the registered Acta Constitutiva
Council members' identification documents
Draft First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains typographical or data variance, the Foundation files a rectification (subsanación) request with the Registry supported by the notarized charter; certified re-issuance is completed within 2 additional business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Social Security Registration (RUC, CSS, MITRADEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Caja de Seguro Social (CSS); Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Formulario RUC at the DGI window or online portal declaring the Foundation's economic activities (restaurant service and condiment supply, ISIC 5610 / NAICS 722511), registered address, and legal representative. Register as employer with CSS and file the company opening notice (aviso de apertura) with MITRADEL; obtain employer account numbers for payroll and social security contributions.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Fundación
Certified copy of the Acta Constitutiva
First Board Resolution appointing the legal representative
Identification of the Council representative
Proof of registered office address
Bank account verification if requested by DGI
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI rejects the RUC application for classification mismatch or missing exhibits, the representative files a corrective sworn statement and resubmits at the same window; CSS and MITRADEL observations are cured by submitting payroll schedules and the employment contract template, generally within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operation Notice and Ancillary Commercial Permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá - Dirección General de Rentas Municipales (or the municipal treasury of the operating district); facilitation through the Ventanilla Única de Inversiones for small and medium enterprises.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación (notice of commercial operation) together with the zoning certificate (uso de suelo), premises lease, and floor plan. Pay the applicable municipal taxes (aviso, business activity tax, signage) and obtain the annual municipal operation card. The application triggers inspection by municipal health and fire officers.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
MINSA preliminary health inspection form
Premises lease or property title
Zoning/land-use certificate
Floor plan and venue capacity description
Fire safety inspection appointment
First Board Resolution confirming the local manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiencies are cured through the municipal subsanación counter within the 10-day response term; if the permit is denied for zoning non-conformity, the Foundation may request a zoning waiver (varianza) or relocate within the approved district and re-file; an appeal lies to the Mayor within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud de Panamá (MINSA) - Dirección General de Salud, Dirección de Regulación Sanitaria, for the sanitary operating permit; Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) for the Registro Sanitario de Alimentos Procesados if packaged condiments are sold wholesale.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento para Establecimientos de Preparación y Expendio de Alimentos (Restaurante), together with the municipal Aviso de Operación and, if applicable, Registro Sanitario de Alimentos Procesados for packaged condiment products.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Cumplimiento Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Low Environmental Impact) - submission of the Formulario Categoría I (Environmental Assessment Registration) and issuance of a Resolución de Aprobación Ambiental; a full EsIA (Category II/III) is not required for a mid-size urban restaurant, subject to load and effluent thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to municipal sewer: pH 6.0-9.0, BOD5 not exceeding 250 mg/L, COD not exceeding 500 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 200 mg/L, fats/oil/grease not exceeding 50 mg/L, per Decreto Ejecutivo No. 343 de 2007 and municipal pre-treatment bylaws; mandatory grease trap and oil separator; kitchen exhaust filtration for cooking vapors; solid waste and recyclables managed under Ley No. 7 de 2022; no ozone-depleting substances under Ley No. 36 de 1999.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (Bomberos Unidos de Panamá) fire-safety certification covering extinguishers, emergency signage, and evacuation plans; SINAPROC structural occupancy inspection and certificate of capacity (aforo); occupational risk clearance under MITRADEL regulations (Resolución No. 011 de 2012, Reglamento de Seguridad, Salud e Higiene en el Trabajo) including workplace risk assessment and staff training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance (Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas); online portal: SIF (Sistema de Facturación Integrado) via https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation: (1) Engage a Panamanian resident Foundation Agent (Agente Residente) as required by Law No. 25 of 1995; (2) File foundation charter with the Registro Público and obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) from the DGI; (3) Complete RUC pre-registration through the DGI's SIF online portal or in person at an Atención al Contribuyente office, submitting the public deed, the agent's identification, and a power of attorney; (4) The DGI issues the RUC (11-digit tax ID) and simultaneously registers the entity for ITBMS where applicable; (5) If the foundation engages in local commercial activities, also obtain a municipal Aviso de Operación and police/general license; ongoing annual franchise tax must be paid to the Registro Público.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope; Private Interest Foundation is subject to a flat annual franchise tax (USD 300 for assets up to USD 10 million; USD 350–400 above that threshold) and is exempt from Panamanian income tax on foreign-source income; Panamanian-source income would be taxed at corporate rates (15% on first USD 1.5 million; 25% above), but the overseas restaurant's operating revenue is sourced abroad and thus outside Panama's territorial net.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' or Panamanian entity classification election exists; the foundation's charter defines whether it is passive (standard, asset-holding only) or commercially active. A PIF may voluntarily elect to register for ITBMS and income tax as an 'empresa' if it derives Panama-source income. Panama has not implemented BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch elections; no elective flow-through treatment, but a foundation legally may be restructured to a sociedad anónima (corporation) via charter amendment, subject to DGI registration updates.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) – Panamanian VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general exemption threshold: every person habitually carrying out taxable transfers of goods or services must register for ITBMS from the first operation. A simplified 'pequeño contribuyente' fixed-tax regime is available for taxpayers with annual gross turnover not exceeding USD 36,000, but a full-service restaurant chain and export activity will not qualify for that simplified regime and must file standard periodic ITBMS returns on a monthly basis.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory fully electronic invoicing through the DGI's SIF (Sistema de Facturación Integrado). All ITBMS-registered businesses must issue e-invoices using a DGI-authorized facturador electrónico (cloud API web service, authorized billing software, or DGI's own web invoicing module) with near-real-time transmission of invoice data to the DGI fiscal platform; no per-invoice digital stamp fee applies; QR code certification on invoices is mandatory for consumer-facing operations such as restaurant POS receipts; all credit notes, debit notes and export invoices must also flow through the SIF clearance API.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating (0% ITBMS) applies to: (i) tangible goods physically exported from Panamanian customs territory, evidenced by customs exit; and (ii) services rendered to non-residents where the service is effectively used or exploited exclusively outside Panama. For this hotpot chain, local dine-in and retail sales in Panama are taxable at 7%; sales of food products (condiments, packaged hotpot sauces, prepared ingredient kits) shipped to the overseas restaurant operation qualify for zero rating when good title passes outside Panama or the goods are physically shipped with customs exit documentation. A formal 'export services' declaration must be filed with DGI where applicable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DUA (Declaración Única Aduanera) presented via Panama's SIGA customs system evidencing physical exit of the goods
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (e-Waybill) evidencing transport to the overseas destination
Commercial invoice (export invoice) issued through the SIF e-invoicing platform with zero-rate indicator
Inward Remittance Certificate (Comprobante de Remesa / bank credit advice) or equivalent SWIFT statement evidencing receipt of foreign-currency export proceeds in a Panama bank account
Contract or purchase order from the overseas affiliate/buyer substantiating the foreign commercial transaction
Packing list and certificate of origin (optional but recommended for food exports)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama's territorial system and export zero-rating are scrutinized via DGI documentary audits; failure to produce the customs and FX-repatriation bundle within the prescribed period results in reversal of the 0% rate and assessment of the 7% ITBMS plus statutory interest (1% per month on the unpaid tax) and fines that may reach 100%–200% of the tax due under the Código Fiscal; deliberately falsified export documentation or sham offshore structures trigger criminal tax fraud and money-laundering charges, retrospective clawback for the 5-year statute-of-limitations window, blacklisting from the Registro Único de Contribuyentes, and disqualification of the Foundation Agent in serious cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama has no traditional central bank or issuer of national paper currency. The United States Federal Reserve is the de facto monetary authority because Panama is a fully dollarized economy and the U.S. dollar is unrestricted legal tender. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the prudential regulator for all licensed banks, trust companies, and financial service providers. The Banco Nacional de Panamá, a state-owned bank, acts as fiscal agent of the Republic and participates in official clearing operations, while the Caja de Ahorros operates as the second state bank. The Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) supervises the public banks and coordinates fiscal policy. For FX and treasury governance, the operative rules derive from SBP agreements and circulars (including AML/CFT Ordinances such as Acuerdo 5-2020), banking practice codified under the Ley Bancaria (Legislative Decree 2 of 2008), and the Commercial and Tax Codes, given the absence of an exchange-control decree.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a complete dollarization regime with full convertibility on both current and capital account transactions. The Panamanian balboa is a nominal accounting unit equal to U.S. dollar at a fixed 1:1 parity and circulates only as domestically minted coinage; all paper currency is U.S. Federal Reserve notes. There are no legal exchange controls, no surrender or conversion requirements, no prior licensing for foreign exchange operations, and no restrictions on profit remittance, capital repatriation, dividend distribution, or cross-border wire settlement for licensed banks. Non-resident investors and Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) may hold, deposit, transfer, and repatriate USD without central bank approvals. The only prudential filters are the SBP's customer due diligence and currency-quality standards for physical cash handling. For taxation, Panama applies a territorial system: a PIF with only foreign-source income (overseas hotpot restaurant operations) is not subject to Panamanian income tax on those revenues, and distributions to non-resident beneficiaries are generally excluded from Panamanian withholding where the underlying wealth is foreign-source; Panamanian-source income, if any, would be assessed at the standard corporate rate of 25%, with 10% withholding on dividends paid to non-residents from Panamanian-source profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender rules in Panama. Exporters, including the group's condiment supply branch that ships hotpot sauces and spices to the overseas restaurant, are not required to convert, repatriate, or surrender hard currency to any government entity. All export receipts may be retained in USD in any SBP-licensed bank, freely transferred abroad, or used to fund intercompany settlement. The only administrative obligations are commercial and customs compliance: an exporter must file the Declaración Única de Importación (DUI) or its export equivalent through the National Customs Authority (Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas), maintain commercial invoices and bills of lading, and report export values for the national statistics regime (SIEX). AML obligations apply to the banking channel: cash exports or wire receipts above USD 10,000 must be traceable to a declared commercial transaction, and the paying bank will require the underlying sales contract, pro-forma invoice, and customs document reference to prevent money-laundering red flags.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility for a PIF Group. Panama does not recognize the European EMI passport and does not issue e-money institution licenses to pure offshore digital wallets. A foreign fintech or digital EMI cannot hold deposits or provide merchant acquiring in Panama without partnering with an SBP-licensed bank or obtaining a niche financial services license from the SBP. Consequently, the Primary Treasury Rail must be a Tier-1 licensed commercial bank; offshore EMIs (e.g., EU-licensed or UK-licensed e-money firms) may be used only as auxiliary aggregation tools for the overseas operating subsidiary's petty cash and local-currency soft currency payments, subject to the group's cash concentration policy and the operating jurisdiction's own EMI authorization. Any EMI holding group client money above USD 10,000 per day must be contractually backed by an SBP-compliant correspondent bank, and the PIF treasury must obtain an annual independent audit of the EMI provider.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed Private Interest Foundation with non-resident founders, physical presence of the founder and at least two foundation council signatories is effectively mandatory at most Tier-1 banks. The SBP's due diligence regime (Acuerdo 5-2020 and the Beneficial Owner Registry Law 23 of 2015, as amended by Law 70 of 2019) requires face-to-face verification or an equivalent digital onboarding capability that very few banks approve for PIFs. In practice, a documented remote opening protocol is available only where the bank has pre-approval for video-call onboarding, the documents are apostilled and notarized by a Panamanian notary, and the entity's file contains a formal legal opinion from a Panamanian law firm confirming the foundation's existence, good standing, and the identity of its council members. Where travel is impossible, the founder may grant a notarized power of attorney to a locally resident professional attorney-in-fact, but the attorney-in-fact cannot obscure the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), and the bank will still conduct an interview with the beneficial owner via secure video. The standard pattern for tier-1 banks is: initial physical interview of the UBO or attorney-in-fact, apostilled corporate package, sworn UBO declaration (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final), followed by hybrid signatory activation within 10-15 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity of the Private Interest Foundation, including undisclosed beneficiaries, protectors, or bearer-style participation certificates
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract of the Foundation Deed (Escritura Pública) registered with the Registro Público de Panamá; Certificate of Existence and Good Standing issued by the Registro Público; sworn UBO Declaration (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final) listing every founder, council member, protector, and beneficiary with passport and tax ID; the foundation regulations (Reglamento) executed before a Panamanian notary; and a formal legal opinion from a licensed Panamanian law firm confirming the entity structure and the absence of bearer instruments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds (SOF) for the initial endowment capital and recurring inbound injections from overseas restaurant profits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn or audited bank statements of the founder or group holding company for the preceding 12 months reflecting the lawful origin of the endowment; certified financial statements of the overseas hotpot restaurant chain; tax clearance certificates or tax filings from the operating jurisdiction; the board resolution of the beneficiary company or foundation council authorizing the capital injection; and an internal SOF memo prepared by the Panamanian fiduciary agent explaining the economic rationale of the wire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive full-service restaurant activity (ISIC 5610) producing POS aggregates and cash deposits that may appear inconsistent with declared revenue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly merchant-acquiring settlement statements from the overseas restaurant's POS provider; reconciled point-of-sale transaction logs and daily sales (Z) reports; municipal operating license (Aviso de Operación or equivalent) of the operating subsidiary; payroll and social security filings for restaurant staff; the group's audited profit and loss showing gross margins consistent with full-service dining; and a treasury policies and procedures manual (TPP) demonstrating cash segregation and bank-sweep rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media exposure of the operating jurisdiction, shareholders, or suppliers (including hotpot condiment importers)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time OFAC, EU, UN, and local consolidated sanctions screening certificates generated by the paying bank; a supplier KYC pack with corporate registry extracts, UBO declarations, trade licenses, and negative-media reports for every material supplier; contractual compliance clauses prohibiting dealings with sanctioned persons or goods; the restaurant chain's supply-chain audit report; and a local counsel opinion on export-import customs compliance in the operating jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation council acting under an undisclosed private mandate or having opaque signatory authority
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized foundation council resolutions appointing the account signatories and treasury officers; a certified copy of the mandate or protector instrument if any; personal references from the relationship manager; fingerprints and passport copies of all signatories certified by the Panamanian Consul; and, when required, a copy of the foundation's internal register of resolutions and the registered attorney-in-fact designation (fiduciario) with the SBP.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections into the PIF are executed by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for nostro-to-nostro) in USD, leveraging Panama's dollarized clearing architecture; no local conversion step is required. The wire must transmit (i) the PIF's registered foundation number or the beneficiary company's tax ID, (ii) a reference to the governing board resolution, (iii) the economic purpose code aligned with IMF BPM6/ECB payment classification: use 'P600' for equity capital investment, 'G100' for a capital contribution to an enterprise, 'P340' for intercompany service transfers, and 'P500' for royalties or license fees where applicable. For sums above USD 10,000, the receiving bank will require a sworn source-of-funds statement, the founder's 12-month bank records, and the beneficiary's tax or incorporation document; for sums above USD 100,000, a Panamanian legal opinion and full UBO declaration are typically demanded. The foundation must also provide the bank's compliance questionnaire (Cuestionario General de Cumplimiento) and undergo the SBP's verification protocol. To avoid frozen funds, the first wire should be preceded by a pre-approval file containing the board resolution, the notarized signatory mandate, the SOF pack, and the deal-specific purpose statement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements from the PIF and its overseas restaurant chain are settled through three preferred rails. First, supplier payments for condiment raw materials, packaging, and equipment are executed by SWIFT MT103 using the 'P340' or 'P500' purpose codes with full invoice, bill of lading, and pro-forma references. Second, for high-value discrete trade shipments of hotpot products, the group issues an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (MT700/MT707) at sight or 30-90 days tenor, with required documents including commercial invoice, full set of clean on-board ocean or air waybill, insurance certificate, sanitary/phytosanitary certificate, and certificate of origin; the LC should be confirmed by a G-SIFI correspondent bank (e.g., JPMorgan or BNY) for USD clearing. Third, steady-state royalty and management-fee payments from the operating subsidiary are swept via intercompany cash-pooling agreements routed through the local subsidiary's bank to the PIF's Panama account, using MT103 with 'P340' and supporting intercompany contracts. The clearing architecture converges on New York USD clearing; daily sweeps are governed by a dual-signatory matrix (two council members above USD 25,000 and a treasury officer above USD 100,000) and a written delegation of authority for the bank's e-banking platform.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC FX forwards (USD against the overseas restaurant's local currency) with tenors up to 12 months, executed with SBP-licensed Tier-1 banks or G-SIFI counterparties, documented under the group's ISDA or local master agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or restricted currencies of the operating jurisdiction, settled in USD on a net difference basis, approved under the group's FX policy and the operating jurisdiction's central bank rules
Cross-currency basis swaps (USD/local currency) for matching intercompany funding and liquidity calendars between the PIF and the operating subsidiary, with cash flow netting via the cash pool
Vanilla OTC currency options (call and put on the operating currency against USD) for protecting budgeted profit remittances, subject to board-approved notional limits and mark-to-market reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Panama Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 June; no statutory grace period; first payment covers the proportional period from incorporation to 31 December of that year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of USD 100. Continued non-payment for three consecutive years triggers suspension of foundation activities and powers; administrative strike-off may be initiated by the Panama Public Registry after five consecutive years of non-payment, with remaining assets passing to the State.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficial Owner Sworn Declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama Public Registry - Beneficial Ownership Section (Registro Público de Panamá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days of the foundation's registration anniversary; annual re-confirmation required; any change in Foundation Council membership or beneficiary status must be updated within 10 business days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file suspends issuance of certificates of good standing and registry status reports; continued non-filing leads to inclusion in the Public Registry's defaulting entity list and may culminate in administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No default statutory audit for Panama Private Interest Foundations. Mandatory independent audit arises under Law 8 of 2010 only if the foundation is commercially active in Panama and reports annual gross revenue equal to or greater than USD 1,000,000, or if it is a regulated financial holding entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for financial statements; IFRS for SMEs permitted for entities below the public-interest and revenue-based threshold.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Resident Agent obtains, at each annual renewal, a signed confirmation from the Foundation Council identifying the Founder, Council Members, Protector (if any), and Beneficiaries. Law 129 of 2020 requires the ultimate beneficial ownership information to be submitted to the Panama Public Registry as an annual sworn declaration. Any transfer of foundation interests or change in beneficiary rights must be reflected in the statutory registers and updated with the Registry within 10 business days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation Council Resolutions and Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 7,500 (only if audit threshold is triggered)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate on annual net taxable income exceeding USD 1,500,000; a reduced 15% rate applies to taxpayers whose annual net taxable income is USD 1,500,000 or less (Articles 699 and 700, Panama Fiscal Code, as amended by Law 52 of 2016 and Cabinet Decree No. 16 of 2016).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies the territoriality principle: foreign-source income of the Private Interest Foundation (PIF), including operating profits of an overseas direct-operated hotpot restaurant and condiment supply chain, is excluded from Panamanian corporate income tax; therefore the effective Panama CIT rate on the overseas restaurant's profit is 0% when all profits are genuinely derived from and managed outside Panama. No statutory tax holiday applies to restaurant operations in Panama; however, 100% deduction is available for payroll and social-contribution costs attributable to any Panamanian backend function, and one-time franchise, licensing, and pre-operating costs are deductible when incurred for Panamanian-source activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 (Declaración de Renta) - annual corporate income tax return for legal entities; required to be filed electronically through the Panama DGI (Dirección General de Ingresos) e-Tax portal available via the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas website; the return must be signed by a duly licensed Panamanian Certified Public Accountant where the taxpayer has revenues above statutory thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing, complemented by 12 monthly informal advance corporate income tax payments (Pagos Mensuales de ISR) calculated by reference to the preceding fiscal year's tax liability and creditable against the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within three months following the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year taxpayer operating in Panama, the statutory filing date is no later than March 31 of the following calendar year; the tax balance must be paid on or before the filing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registration of the foundation's RUC (Registro Unico de Contribuyentes), legal name, domicile, economic activity code (ISIC 5610), and fiscal-year start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PIF must register with the DGI using its Panamanian foundation certificate (Certificado de Fundación); if the PIF has no Panamanian-source income, it files a zero-return with a territorial-source disclosure statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate worldwide gross income shown on the deemed profit basis, including gross sales of food and condiment products, franchise and royalty receipts, and financial income, before cost deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each item, a domiciliary of Panama must classify the country where the services, sale, or licensing activity gave rise to income; income derived from overseas hotpot restaurant operations is not Panamanian-source and is reported on the territorial exclusion lines rather than the taxable line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 - Exempt Income and Foreign-Source Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of income sourced and taxed outside Panama; this line operationalizes the territoriality principle and excludes foreign operating profit of the overseas restaurant chain.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a supporting schedule with foreign profit and loss statements, foreign corporate tax returns, bank statements, and management accounts evidencing that the hotpot restaurant management decisions, customer contracts, and point-of-sale merchant acquiring functions are performed in the host jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 - Deductions and Cost of Sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All statutory deductions and cost of goods sold including food ingredient imports, condiment production costs, payroll, rent, utilities, marketing, depreciation, and financing costs attributable to Panamanian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses directly related to Panamanian-source income are deductible; expenses allocated to the overseas restaurant operation are neither deductible against Panama income nor allowable as a direct offset because such income is already outside the territorial tax net.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10 - Net Taxable Income (Renta Neta Gravable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panamanian-source gross income reduced by allowable domestic deductions; this is the base to which the 15% or 25% rate is applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a pure overseas restaurant PIF, this line is zero; the taxpayer nevertheless completes the entire form for filing-compliance integrity and to avoid indefinite loss of filing history.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 12 - Tax Calculated at Applicable Rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the headline tax on net taxable income at the 15% reduced rate for taxable income up to USD 1,500,000 or the 25% rate for any excess above USD 1,500,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show a zero result where the taxable base is zero; provide a separate memorandum outlining the worldwide foreign-source profit and the equivalent host-country tax paid to substantiate the zero effective Panama rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for monthly ISR prepayments, foreign tax credits available under a DTA, and any withholding credits obtained on Panamanian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits derived from foreign-source restaurant taxes cannot be credited against Panamanian CIT because Panama does not tax foreign income; they are disclosed only for informational purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 20 - Balance Due or Credit to Offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final settlement amount: tax determined minus prepayments and credits; this amount is payable with the return and is subject to interest where paid after the statutory deadline.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Submit the return even with a zero balance; non-filing of any annual return, including a zero territorial return, still exposes the foundation to Registry and DGI penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 110 triggers a fine of USD 50 to USD 500 (Articles 711 and 712, Fiscal Code) together with default interest of 1% per month on any unpaid tax; failure to file after formal administrative demand may lead to embargo of bank accounts, closure of the establishment, and In fiscal-evasion cases, criminal prosecution; the DGI also may impose an increase of up to 100% of the omitted tax for non-filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% for dividends and distributions paid out of profits already subject to Panamanian corporate income tax; 10% for dividends and distributions paid out of income that was not subject to Panamanian corporate income tax, including foreign-source income exempt under the territoriality principle (Articles 733-735, Fiscal Code, as amended). Beneficiaries of a Private Interest Foundation receiving distributions are subject to the same rates; foundation distributions of the original subscribed capital, however, retain the character of non-taxable capital restitution where documented.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where the overseas host jurisdiction applies a dividend or royalty withholding tax and the PIF seeks relief under a Panama double-tax treaty (e.g., Mexico, Republic of Korea, Singapore, Portugal, Barbados, Spain, Qatar, The Netherlands, when in force), the protocol is: (i) obtain a Certificate of Fiscal Residencia (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from the DGI by demonstrating the foundation's incorporation and effective management in Panama; (ii) submit the certificate, together with the relevant treaty-residency article and a beneficial-ownership declaration, to the withholding agent in the host jurisdiction before the remittance is made; (iii) record the reduced withholding rate on the host-country remittance form and retain the certificate for the Panamanian file; and (iv) in case the host tax authority denies treaty relief, pursue a refund application or invoke the Mutual Agreement Procedure (MAP) under the applicable DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Panama withholding applies only to Panamanian-source payments: a 12.5% final withholding generally applies to royalties, technical-assistance fees, commissions, and certain interest paid to non-residents; interest paid on qualified external loans to foreign banks may benefit from a reduced effective treatment where the lender is registered with the DGI. Under Panama's DTA network, typical negotiated limits are 5% to 15% on dividends, 5% to 10% on interest, and 5% to 10% on royalties; in the absence of treaty coverage, foreign-sourced royalties paid between the overseas operating company and the Panamanian PIF remain outside Panama's territorial withholding net.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File documentation applies where the aggregate value of controlled transactions between the PIF and related parties, including royalties or management fees charged to an overseas hotpot operating affiliate, exceeds USD 1,000,000 (B/. 1,000,000) per fiscal period; an annual related-party transaction information return is required when aggregate controlled transactions exceed USD 250,000, pursuant to Executive Decree No. 235 of 2018 and the OECD-aligned transfer pricing chapter of the Panama Fiscal Code.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not maintain a separate statutory Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to UAE ESR; substance requirements operate through (i) general anti-avoidance and anti-shell provisions permitting the DGI to recharacterize transactions lacking economic purpose; (ii) the tax-haven and preferential-regime list of Cabinet Decree No. 56 of 1971, which disables the territorial exemption where the substance test is failed; (iii) the beneficial-ownership statutory framework of Law 70 of 2019, requiring filing of ultimate beneficial owners with the Registry; and (iv) limitation-of-benefits clauses in Panama's DTAs. The overseas hotpot PIF must maintain real asset ownership or real active management of the brand and condiment-supply IP, hold board meetings, keep complete accounting records in Panama or accessible in Panama, and demonstrate that the foundation is not merely a mail-dropping shell in order to preserve territorial exemption and treaty access.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mischaracterizing Panamanian-source catering or local condiment sales as foreign-source income; intentionally omitting Panamanian-source revenue from Form 110; or structuring final tax liquidation to exploit the territorial exemption while operating in Panama without registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 100% to 300% of the evaded tax (Articles 106 and 713, Fiscal Code), default interest at 1% per month, late-filing fines from USD 50 to USD 500, closure of establishments, and criminal prosecution for defraudación fiscal under the Fiscal Code and the criminal procedure applicable to fiscal crimes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members are not liable for the PIF's debts in the ordinary course, but Panama courts and the DGI pierce the foundation veil where the entity is used for fraud, evasion, or money laundering; signatories may incur personal civil restitution, asset attachments, travel bans, disqualification from serving as directors of Panamanian regulated entities, and imprisonment if fraudulent intent is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Private Interest Foundation with no genuine management, no Panamanian administrative staff, no accounting records, and no actual control of the overseas hotpot restaurant and condiment supply chain while claiming the territorial exemption on multi-million-dollar foreign revenue; excessive reliance on nominee council and confidential formation agents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may disregard the foundation as a sham, reallocate foreign-source income as Panamanian-source on the basis of management location, reassess tax at 25% with additional penalties of 100% to 300% and monthly 1% interest; Panama Law 70 of 2019 imposes fines on entities filing false or incomplete beneficial-ownership declarations, and a landmark non-compliance case can trigger registry cancellation, adverse FATF/Gafilat references, and revocation of the PIF's license to operate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors are individually exposed to administrative penalties and disqualification from holding office in Panama-regulated entities; where the shell structure is used to conceal assets or launder proceeds, piercing the veil results in personal liability for civil restitution, seizure of personal assets, travel bans, and criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Deficiencies in Restaurant Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating overseas hotpot restaurant merchant acquiring and POS settlement flows through the PIF's accounts without documented customer due diligence, beneficial-ownership identification, source-of-funds analysis, or suspicious-transaction reporting; processing disproportionate volumes of cash from condiment distribution and franchise transactions with related parties without audit evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Panama's AML/CFT obligations under Law 23 of 2015 and related DNFBP regulations exposes the foundation to administrative fines of up to USD 1,000,000 per infraction, freezing and confiscation of funds, cancellation of the financial or commercial license, and criminal money-laundering prosecution carrying imprisonment of 5 to 12 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members, compliance officers, and beneficial owners face personal criminal liability where willful blindness is proven; the criminal court may impose travel bans, provisional detention, personal fines, asset-confiscation orders, and permanent bans from holding AML-regulated positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Cross-Border Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging inflated royalties or condiment-supply margins from the overseas operating affiliate to the Panamanian PIF without arm's-length benchmarking, or failing to file the annual related-party transaction information return and Local File/Master File once the USD 1,000,000 threshold is exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may make transfer pricing adjustments recharacterizing the profit in the host jurisdiction, assess the resulting Panamanian tax at 25% (or the applicable reduced rate on reassessed Panamanian-source income), impose penalties of 100% to 300% of the adjustment amount, add 1% monthly default interest, and deny the foundation beneficial ownership of the hotpot brand or condiment IP licensed abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the foundation council who sign and approve artificial pricing documentation are jointly liable for the unpaid difference after veil-piercing; in aggravated cases of egregious mispricing, the same conduct is prosecuted as tax evasion, subjecting signatories to imprisonment, travel bans, civil restitution, and disqualification from serving on boards of Panamanian commercial entities.
